newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures end mixed.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed on Tuesday with early-maturing contracts losing on weak sentiment and late-maturing contracts rising on a technical rebound, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday low of 3,106 yuan ($374) per tonne, losing 113 yuan. It opened at 3,200 and hit a high of 3,300 yuan per tonne.
July closed unchanged at 3,447, November fell 89 to 3,122, the January 1998 contract rose two to 3,160 and March put on 10 to 3,150 per tonne.
Combined volume rose to 22,400 tonnes from 19,000 tonnes.
Soybean opened higher and profit-taking pushed the prices to fall for most of the session, traders said.
"Early-maturing contracts met strong selling pressure today due to weak market sentiment," one trader said.
"But late-maturing contracts rose today due to sharp falls over the past few days," he added.
Traders said soybeans would meet selling pressure in coming sessions in the absence of demand over the summer months.
"The general outlook for soybeans is not too good in the short term," a second trader said.
